images.caption: Derelict goods wagons at St Johns: The Isle of Man Railway through St Johns had already been abandoned for some years when these wagons were photographed in 1971, but the Manx Northern branch to Foxdale, upon which these wagons are standing, had been abandoned for much longer. The branch line passed under the road bridge shown here, and continued to Foxdale.

images.caption: St. Johns Station St. Johns was an important station on the Isle of Man Railway, for it was where the lines from Douglas to Peel, and to Ramsey, divided.  It was also the junction for the Foxdale branch.  Here Locomotive No 8 calls with an afternoon train to Ramsey.

images.caption: Abandoned coaching stock at St. John's, Isle of Man When the Peel and Ramsey lines of the Isle of Man Railway closed, redundant coaches were dumped at the erstwhile St. John's station.  Needless to say, it was not long before they attracted the attantion of vandals.
